llm.summary: This is a straightforward learning-distillation skill that only uses disclosed file-reading or web-fetching when the user provides material to process.

dimensions.detail: Reading a provided local file path or fetching a provided URL is proportionate for this skill, but users should be aware those tools can access the specific material they ask it to process.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package inspected is a single Markdown skill file with no executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, or bundled code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill has broad natural-language triggers such as "distill this" and "extract the framework from," which could cause surprise activation in some hosts, but the runtime behavior remains scoped to processing user-supplied material.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, memory writes, privilege escalation, command execution, background workers, or credential handling were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to convert pasted text, files, URLs, or domain names into a structured learning framework, and the declared Read and WebFetch capabilities fit that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want a structured learning aid for text, files, and URLs. Be mindful that giving it a local path or URL asks the agent to read or fetch that material, and mixed-language inputs may produce Chinese output by default.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad "distill this" trigger is a real usability caveat for accidental activation, but it is aligned with the skill's distillation purpose and does not introduce hidden or unrelated authority.
[SQP-1] expected: The "extract the framework from" trigger is also broad, but the artifact only directs the agent to classify the user's provided input and process it using disclosed tools.
[SQP-3] expected: The mixed-input Chinese output rule affects language preference and may be inconvenient, but it is an output-format choice rather than a security or privilege concern.
